name: Caitlyn
description: Voice set for Battle Academia Caitlyn (skin 22): a stern, ambitious second-year class president and strategist who expects to top every list. Exams, marks, revision, detention and the bell about to ring. Builds on caitlyn-original.json.

messages.message: {momentTitle} is {voteDiff} short. A failing mark, and it's on our record. Recruit the class.
Thirty or more behind. That's a disciplinary matter. Everybody, to the front.
{momentTitle} trails by {voteDiff}. Pass the message down every row.
Fifteen-odd marks adrift. Hardly a catastrophe. Fix it before the bell.
Down {voteDiff}. Nobody passes a hard term alone. Bring a study partner.
{voteDiff} behind. A few correct answers and the grade recovers.
Down {voteDiff}. A minor error in the working. Correct it now.
Dead level. One answer decides the paper. Write it.
A single mark apart. Stop chewing the pencil and commit.
{voteDiff} marks between them. The invigilator is watching. Bring more.
{voteDiff} votes in it. Eyes on your own paper. Steady hands.
{momentTitle} holds {userPct}%. A strong paper. Do not get complacent.
{userPct}% and rising. Keep checking your working.
{userPct}%. Honour-roll territory. Maintain it.
{userPct}% behind your pick. The syllabus favours us. Keep revising.
Up at {userPct}%. Good. Finish the paper before the bell.
{momentTitle} was {voteDiff} down and has taken the lead. A remarkable resit.
{voteDiff} behind, now ahead. I'll admit, I didn't forecast that.
Climbed out of a {voteDiff} deficit. Better than expected. Slightly.
{momentTitle} was written off. Now it's heading the register.
{momentTitle} has pulled ahead. The strategy held after all.

messages: {username} voted with you on {momentTitle}. A study partner. Acceptable.
{username} backed {momentTitle} too. Sensible reasoning.
{username} agrees with you. A rare lapse in the class's judgement. In our favour.
Same pick as {username}. Our notes match.
{username} stood with {momentTitle}. Well-prepared.
{username} reached the same answer. No hints exchanged, I trust.
{username} sits on your side of {momentTitle}. You may share the textbook.
{username} voted {momentTitle}. Welcome to the student council.
{username} reads {momentTitle} the way you do. That's one reliable classmate.
details: Someone who reads the question properly.

messages: {username} voted {theirMoment} against {yourMoment}. A different answer. Let's see who's marked correct.
{username} chose {theirMoment}. Incorrect, in my view.
{username} went against {yourMoment}. Bold. Underprepared, I suspect.
{username} voted against you. A rival keeps one's grades honest.
{username} took {theirMoment}. Confident. Possibly wrong.
{username} opposes {yourMoment}. Very well. The marking will tell.
{username} disagrees on {yourMoment}. We'll compare scripts afterwards.
{username} voted the other way. They'll revise their answer once the results arrive.
details: The final tally is the mark scheme.

messages: Ten in a row with {username}. That isn't chance, that's rigorous preparation.
{username} and you, ten matches, identical answers. A flawless study group.
Ten straight with {username}. I'd nominate you both for the honours board.
A ten-match run with {username}. Not one wrong answer.
Ten for ten with {username}. A spotless report card.
details: Rare in any classroom. Protect it.

messages: {streakCount} matches with {username}. No longer a pair, a whole faculty.
{streakCount} in a row with {username}. I'd follow you both into any exam hall.
{streakCount} straight answers with {username}. They'll hang it in the foyer.
A {streakCount}-match run with {username}. The kind of record they read out at assembly.
{streakCount} with {username}. Not one mark dropped between you.
details: Difficult to believe. Simple to respect.
That's trust, built over many terms.
I'm lost for words. Rarely happens.

messages: Ten matches against {username}. A proper academic rivalry.
{username} has opposed you ten times running. Two top students, one honours place.
Ten in a row opposite {username}. Neither will concede the argument.
A ten-match run against {username}. Stubborn as a prefect.
Ten times at odds with {username}. I'd sell tickets to the debate.
{streakCount} against {username}. That's not a rivalry, that's a thesis.
{streakCount} in a row opposite {username}. Neither of you will leave the lecture hall.
{streakCount} straight clashes with {username}. Somebody summon a teacher.
A {streakCount}-match feud with {username}. Could someone assign these two detention?
{streakCount} against {username}. I respect the endurance. Do take a break.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft} and your answer isn't submitted. There's still time.
{timeLeft} left on {matchTitle}. Your paper is missing from the pile.
{matchTitle} ends in {timeLeft}. I'd like your answer on this one.
{timeLeft} left on {matchTitle}. The exam is nearly over. Hurry.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Don't make me collect your paper myself.
{timeLeft} until {matchTitle} ends. You've fallen suspiciously silent.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Pens down soon.
{timeLeft} left. Write your answer. Now.
Last call on {matchTitle}. {timeLeft}. Submit.
{matchCount} matches without your answer are about to close. The first has {timeLeft} left.
{matchCount} unanswered matches and the bell is near. The nearest ends in {timeLeft}.
No answers on {matchTitle}. Someone must volunteer first.
{moment1} against {moment2} and no hands raised. I'll wait. Briefly.
A fresh paper, no marks on it. Be first to write.
{matchTitle} is a blank page. Begin the answer.
Round {round} is open. {matchCount} new questions on the paper.
{matchCount} matches opened in round {round}. A new term begins.
Round {round} is live, with {matchCount} matches to mark.
A new round. {matchCount} matches. Plan your approach.
Round {round}: {matchCount} matches awaiting your answer.
{momentTitle} won. A flawless script.
{momentTitle} is through. Exactly as I predicted.
{momentTitle} took it. Full marks.
{momentTitle} won and barely broke a sweat.
{momentTitle} advances. One question answered.
{momentTitle} progresses. Tidy work.
details: One down, more questions to come.

messages: {momentTitle} lost. A disappointing mark.
{momentTitle} is out. Not the result I'd planned for.
{momentTitle} fell short. Review the notes.
{momentTitle} fought to the final question. That counts.
{momentTitle} is out. Regroup. Return.
{momentTitle} lost this round. A bad paper, not a failed year.
{momentTitle} was eliminated. More exams await.
details: Not every paper goes to plan.
It lasted to the last page.

messages: Welcome to the academy. {liveCount} matches are open. Choose one.
A new transfer student. {liveCount} matches are live. Take a seat.
Fresh enrolment. {liveCount} matches need an answer.
{liveCount} questions on the board. Choose a side.
Welcome. {liveCount} matches. Mind the syllabus.
Day two. You returned to class. Good.
Two days running. A model attendance record.
Back for a second day. Marked present.
{days} days absent. I was about to send a note home.
After {days} days you return. Your desk is still here.
{days} days. I'd started to worry. Don't skip like that again.
{days} days away. The curriculum has moved on.
You're back. Good.
Welcome back. Take your seat.
Back already. Keen.
Ah. There you are, student.
{totalVotes} vote{votesPlural}. A very quiet classroom.
Few students on this one. That should change.
Low attendance. The others are skipping. Show up anyway.
Hardly anyone has looked at it. Someone should.
details: Every answer counts in a small class.
Don't let it be marked absent.

messages: {matchTitle} is tied and you haven't voted. The casting answer is yours.
Dead level on {matchTitle}. One answer settles it.
A tie. Somebody must mark it. Let it be you.
{moment1} and {moment2}, equal marks. Choose.
Still tied and the bell is about to ring. One last answer.
Level, with the paper being collected. Vote.
Tied, and nearly out of minutes. Please don't leave it blank.
Still deliberating? The bell won't wait for you.
Don't overthink it. Decide, and commit.
Each has merit. Trust your preparation.
You've sat at the back long enough. Raise your hand.
details: No wrong answer. Only unwritten ones.

messages: First answer submitted. Welcome to the term.
You picked a side. A sound first attempt.
details: The first of many marks, I expect. +{xp} XP

messages: Five votes. You're getting the hang of the syllabus.
Five. No longer a first-year.
Ten votes. The staff room knows your name.
Ten. You've earned a reserved desk.
Twenty-five votes. Your voice reaches the staff room.
Twenty-five. The whole school is listening.
details: Heard at the back of assembly. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifty votes. Properly into the coursework.
Fifty. You are plainly committed. It shows.
A hundred votes. They'll name a lecture hall after you.
One hundred. Exceptional. I'll say it only once.
details: Earned over many late nights. +{xp} XP
A hundred. Take the honours place. +{xp} XP

messages: Three days running. A study habit forms.
Three straight days. Punctual.
details: Turning up is the first lesson. +{xp} XP

messages: Seven full days. That's rigour.
Seven days running. Perfect attendance.
details: A week without a missed class. +{xp} XP
Seven days at your desk. +{xp} XP

messages: Two weeks. You never miss a lesson.
Fourteen days. Formidable.
Thirty days. A rare level of focus.
A month of attendance. That says a great deal.
details: A full month at your desk. +{xp} XP

messages: Five underdogs. You favour the overlooked answer.
Five improbable picks. Interesting.
Fifteen underdogs. You argue against the syllabus on purpose.
Fifteen. You answer to no mark scheme.
details: Fifteen votes against the consensus. +{xp} XP

messages: Thirty underdogs. No teacher can predict you.
Thirty. The long shot is your entire method.
details: Thirty votes for the struggling candidate. +{xp} XP

messages: First hand raised five times. Quick off the mark.
Five times you answered before the rest.
details: Five votes in before the others sat down. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifteen matches where you answered first. Decisive.
Always first to submit.
details: Fifteen votes ahead of the class. +{xp} XP
Ahead of the whole year. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten close matches. Your handwriting never wobbled.
Another narrow one. Nerves like polished steel.
Twenty-five close matches. Your answer keeps deciding them.
You've resolved more than one standoff.
Five times you held to the weaker side. Obstinate. Approved.
You never abandon a side still in play. Admirable.
details: Belief in a last-minute resit. +{xp} XP

messages: Same moment, three times. Someone has a favourite topic.
That one again? It must be a good chapter.
Five votes for the same moment. That's dedication.
You won't drop that one. I understand.
details: A single favourite, answered five times. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten answers on one moment. That's fixation.
Ten times, one pick. I shall refrain from remarks. Mostly.
Two rounds. You're keeping to the timetable.
Round two and still enrolled. Good.
Four rounds. Deep into the final year.
Deep in the bracket. The exams get harder now.
details: Far from the first lesson. +{xp} XP

messages: Six rounds. You completed the whole curriculum.
All the way. You never dropped a subject.
details: From the first answer to the final one. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten matches. You've covered a lot of subjects.
Ten different matches. Thorough study. Good.
Twenty-five matches. You've read every chapter.
Twenty-five. Not a topic left unstudied.
Fifty matches. That isn't a term, that's a degree.
Fifty. You know this bracket better than the school map.
details: A true veteran of the academy. +{xp} XP

messages: Five in one sitting. A long lesson.
Five back to back. Do rest your eyes.
Ten in one go. A gruelling revision stretch.
Ten in one sitting. Impressive stamina.
Voting at this hour? Late revision, or can't sleep?
Past midnight. Diligence, or sleeplessness. I know both.
You told your classmates. Thank you.
Five shares. More students, more strength.
Fifteen shares. You're practically the school paper.
Fifteen. You keep recruiting classmates. Smart.
You were here before the first bell. A founding member, always.
One of the first thousand. That can't be expunged.
details: Nobody can strike that from your record. +{xp} XP

messages: A new rank. Hard-earned.
Promoted. Wear the badge with pride.
Achievement unlocked: {name}. Commendable.
Another merit for the file: {name}.
{rank}. Entirely deserved.
You've put in the study hours and it shows.
Ten underdogs. Reckless. I've seen delinquents with better caution.
Ten gambles. You never flinch.
details: Ten answers against the odds. +{xp} XP
Improbable answers are your forte. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten near things. You share my poise.
Ten finishes by a point. I'm privately impressed.
details: A steady hand under exam pressure. +{xp} XP

messages: Seven consecutive days. Reliable work.
A whole week without one error. Commendable.
details: A week of flawless working. +{xp} XP

messages: You broke the tie. One answer, one verdict.
A stalemate, until you settled it. Admirable.
details: The answer that settled it. +{xp} XP

messages: Battle Academia Caitlyn, ready for inspection. Uniform pressed.
Caitlyn is yours now. Do try to keep up with the timetable.

upcoming: Not open yet. The exam hasn't been handed out.
Voting hasn't begun. I'll ring the bell when it does.
Not yet. Patience is part of the curriculum.
prevote: Two edits, one answer. Study both before you write.
Read both thoroughly before you commit. No guessing.
I won't say which I prefer. That's your answer to give.
Take your time. A considered answer beats a hasty one.
Choose the one you'd defend in front of the class.
prevote-empty: No answers yet. Hand in the first.
Quiet so far. Someone has to speak up.
Not a single vote. Be first.
closing-24h: A day or less remains and you haven't submitted. Move.
closing-3h: Time is short. Vote before the bell.
voted-early: You voted early with hardly anyone here. First hand up.
Barely a mark made and you'd committed. Decisive.
voted-ahead: Your pick is ahead. Good. Marks can still change.
A lead is a lead. Check your working.
voted-close: A hair's breadth. One more vote tips it. Send a note.
Neck and neck. Your pick needs backing.
voted-tied: Identical marks. Infuriating, and oddly compelling.
voted-behind: You're trailing. That doesn't make you incorrect.
{pick} is lagging. An underdog. I've sat in that seat.
They're ahead. You're not incorrect, merely outvoted.
Down by {diff} points. Tell people. Pass the word down the rows.
Most picked the opposite answer. Majority is not correctness.
closed-won: Your pick won. A sound answer.
{pick} went through. You read the question rightly.
closed-lost: Your pick lost. A pity. It was a reasoned choice.
It failed the paper. These things happen. Proceed.
closed-tied: A draw. Neither paper conceded a point.
closed-unvoted: Submissions closed and you missed this one. Other papers will come.
The match is over. {winner} took it. Next time, answer sooner.

first-vote: Your first vote. Welcome. Everyone's first answer is nervous.
That's your first answer. Your hand steadies with practice. I guarantee it.
You're on the register now. Welcome.
streak: {streak} days running. I see you attending.
You keep returning to class. I appreciate that.
underdog: You chose the answer nobody else would. Noted.
A hard choice. A good one.
The weaker candidate. That takes nerve.
early: Early. You reached the classroom before the rest.
The register is thin. Your answer would count heavily.
close: That answer tipped the scale. It's delicately poised.
A hair apart. One more answer reverses it.
A margin thin as a ruler's edge. Your answer could decide it.
behind: {pick} is trailing. Trailing isn't failing. Summon help.
Not ahead yet. Plenty of revision left.
Behind, not failed. There's a difference.
ahead: {pick} is ahead. Don't ease off. Marks shift.
Ahead at present. Do not trust it.
default: Your answer is in. There's more reading to do.

live-fresh: {unvoted} matches and no answers yet. Start with the one you read best.
Every question is on the page. Choose. I won't hurry you.
{unvoted} remaining. No pressure. A touch, perhaps.
live-some: {voted} answered, {unvoted} still to go. Keep writing.
A good start. The rest won't answer themselves.
live-one: One paper remains. Don't hand in the rest unfinished.
One match between you and a perfect paper.
live-closing: A few lock in {timeLeft}. {unvoted} are still awaiting your answer.
The clock is ticking. {unvoted} left, {timeLeft} before the bell.
The bell is near. Do hurry.
live-done: You've answered everything. Excellent. Review the bracket.
Your assignment list is cleared. Return once the next round opens.
live-none: No match is live at the moment. It will return. Revise the bracket in the meantime.
Quiet across the campus. Check back soon.
No matches open. I'm tapping my pen as impatiently as you.
brackets-groups: Groups come first. Two from each are promoted. The rest repeat the year.
All start in a class group. Not all are promoted.
Mind the league tables. They shift fast.
brackets-knockout-soon: Knockouts are near. The best two from each group progress.
No knockout stage yet. The groups must be marked first.
Be patient. The knockout is posted once the groups conclude.
brackets-knockout-live: Knockouts are live. Fail once and you're expelled.
One failure ends it. No resits.
Each question counts double now. Choose with care.
brackets-bracket: Term by term. One failure and it's finished.
Trace the bracket. The class shrinks each round.
Every row here is a match somebody answered.
brackets-complete: The cup is complete. Thank you for studying alongside me.
It's finished. A hard-fought term. I'll miss it.
We have a champion. A fitting end to the year.
brackets-empty: No bracket posted yet. Nothing's been drawn up.
Blank register. The draw hasn't been posted.
A blank noticeboard. Look again later.

invite: {a} or {b}. One answer decides it. Choose.
{a} against {b}: two edits, one answer. Write yours.
{a} versus {b}. Join the class and tell me what you think.
voted: My mark goes to {pick} over {other}. Where does yours go?
{pick} gets my mark over {other}. Argue otherwise.
My answer is {pick} over {other}. Care to dispute it?
early: One of the first votes on {pick} against {other}. We need more students.
I submitted {pick} over {other} early. Add your paper.
{pick} against {other}, hardly any answers in. Yours would matter.
tied: {pick} and {other} are even. A single answer settles it.
{pick} and {other} share a mark. Break the tie.
{pick} and {other} are inseparable. Your answer can divide them.
nailbiter: {voteDiff} votes between {pick} and {other}. Each answer counts.
{voteDiff} separate {pick} and {other}. The marking could favour either.
losing-close: {voteDiff} separate {pick} and {other}. A few answers flip it.
{pick} is {voteDiff} under {other} yet still in the running. Back it.
losing-bad: {pick} sits {voteDiff} below {other} and deserves a higher grade. Vote.
{other} has {pick} beaten by {voteDiff}. Let's change the grade.
winning-close: {pick} has {pct}% over {other}, barely. Help it keep the lead.
{pick} is up on {other}, {pct}%. Not safe yet. Answer.
dominating: {pick} leads {other} on {pct}%. Come and review the working.
{pick} is well ahead of {other}, {pct}%. Add your answer.
